html:
In December 1969 drillers found the Ekofisk oil field in the Norwegian part of the North Sea. It was the start of Norway's oil age.

Oil companies had drilled for years with little luck and almost gave up. Stavanger became the base of the new industry. Ekofisk began producing in 1971. Norway decided early that the state would keep control: it set up the oil company Statoil, now Equinor, in 1972 and taxed the profits heavily.

Oil and gas turned a country of fishing, shipping and forestry into one of the richest in the world. To avoid wasting the money, the state paid much of it into the oil fund. The offshore industry still employs many, though Norway also leads in electric cars. The find came within months of the oil shocks that raised its value.
